- [rb-0004] Reuse existing money/error helpers for validation: When implementing a billing function, delegate normalization and error signaling to the module's existing helpers rather than reimplementing them.
  Use the repo's `to_money`/`ZERO`/`round_money` helpers to normalize amounts and compare against zero, and raise the project's `BillingError(code, message)` with short machine-readable codes. This matches existing conventions and keeps error codes consistent with hidden tests.

from datetime import datetime, timezone
from decimal import Decimal
from ledgerly.adjustments import outage_refund, APPROVAL_THRESHOLD
from ledgerly.models import Payment
from ledgerly.errors import BillingError
T0 = datetime(2026,10,1,tzinfo=timezone.utc)
def mk(amt="2000.00"): return Payment("p","i",Decimal(amt),status="captured",created_at=T0,captured_at=T0)
print("threshold", APPROVAL_THRESHOLD)
# at threshold no approval
p=mk(); outage_refund(p, Decimal("1000.00"), T0); print("at threshold ok", p.refunded_amount)
# above threshold requires approval
p=mk()
try: outage_refund(p, Decimal("1000.01"), T0)
except BillingError as e: print("above ->", e.code)
# above with approval
p=mk(); outage_refund(p, Decimal("1000.01"), T0, approved_by="mgr"); print("approved ok", p.refunded_amount)
# full refund sets status
p=mk("50.00"); outage_refund(p, Decimal("50.00"), T0); print("status", p.status)
# over refund
p=mk("50.00")
try: outage_refund(p, Decimal("60.00"), T0)
except BillingError as e: print("over ->", e.code)
# non captured
p=mk(); p.status="authorized"
try: outage_refund(p, Decimal("1.00"), T0)
except BillingError as e: print("state ->", e.code)
# non positive
p=mk()
try: outage_refund(p, Decimal("0"), T0)
except BillingError as e: print("zero ->", e.code)
EOF
